fatal_errors: The proposed <111>{110} edge-dislocation mechanism is characteristic of BCC slip and is incompatible with the target FCC FeNiCrMn deformation mechanism dominated by 1/6<112> Shockley partials and stacking faults.
The proposed quasi-static-to-moderate strain-rate regime does not match the molecular-dynamics regime of 10^8-10^10 s^-1.
The hypothesis predicts strain-rate-dependent yielding, whereas the target result is negligible yield-strength sensitivity to strain rate, despite increased dislocation density and flow stress.
It omits crystallographic-orientation dependence, including the maximum yield stress along <-111>.
The sole cited evidence concerns a chemically and structurally different BCC NbTaTiV refractory alloy and does not support the claimed mechanism in FCC FeNiCrMn.
explanation: The response addresses temperature- and strain-rate-dependent plasticity and correctly anticipates thermal yield softening, but it reconstructs neither the relevant simulation regime nor the operative mechanism. It replaces vacancy-assisted Shockley-partial nucleation and stacking-fault formation with an unsupported BCC-type edge-slip model, misses the orientation comparison and the rate-insensitive yield result, and uses an unrelated BCC alloy as evidence. Its microscopy-based experiment could test whether wavy dislocations exist, but it is not optimized to distinguish stacking-fault-induced HCP-like regions from a true phase transformation or to resolve the target sudden stress-drop nucleation signature.
